_comment: Reviewed-but-not-now decisions for tools/check_dependency_freshness.py. Each entry needs deferredLatest and reason; it expires by itself once the registry passes that release. A permanent policy belongs on the declaring line as `# freshness-hold:` instead.

futures-util.reason: Exact pin =0.3.33 in crates/linux/Cargo.toml, a manifest this fork keeps identical to upstream. Re-checked 2026-11-21: upstream/main e8934a5e still pins =0.3.33 (git grep futures-util upstream/main -- crates/linux/Cargo.toml) and crates.io latest is still 0.3.34 (published 2026-08-11). No deny.toml or changelog reason is recorded; the only ground is ownership, and the Linux crate does not compile on the Windows host that gates this fork (docs/fork/DECISIONS.md, ADR-006 point 3 and ADR-013).

zbus.reason: crates/linux pins zbus =5.19.0, and so does upstream/main e8934a5e (re-checked 2026-11-21). deny.toml records why: 5.19 is the newest release with the blocking API the Linux adapter uses. Checked 2026-11-21 against crates.io metadata: 5.19.0 (2026-08-09) is the newest 5.x and lists a `blocking-api` feature; 6.5.0 (2026-11-20) lists none, and crates/linux/src has 27 `zbus::blocking` uses. The zbus 6 changelog itself was not read. The three RUSTSEC-2026-0370..0372 ignores go away when upstream moves the adapter to zbus 6 (docs/fork/DECISIONS.md, ADR-013).

actions/download-artifact.reason: Pinned at v8.0.1 in release.yml and release-dry-run.yml, upstream-owned workflow files this fork keeps identical to upstream on the pinned lines; the floor moves when the fork syncs upstream. Re-checked 2026-11-21: upstream/main e8934a5e still pins v8.0.1 and the latest release is still 8.0.2 (docs/fork/DECISIONS.md, ADR-006 point 3 and ADR-013).
